clue.text: Sob stuff from sailor, by the way

parts.note: a path is a way or track
OS is an ordinary seaman, a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman's mawkish tale, mentioned in passing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by the way' looks like a throwaway aside; here 'by' just puts the sailor beside the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Sob stuff is sentimental material meant to stir pity, which is exactly that quality in art or speech.

clue.text: A definition — lowering constant speed

indicators.note: in a down entry, lowering moves a letter further down

parts.note: clarity is sharpness or definition of an image
C is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

explanation.surface: A precise definition: lowering a constant speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lowering' moves the C two places down CLARITY to make LACRITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Alacrity is brisk eagerness, quickness in responding.

clue.text: Be sick of entertaining the Spanish premier's wife

indicators.note: entertaining guests means holding them inside

parts.note: to hate is to be sick of
el is Spanish for the
PM is the Prime Minister, the premier

explanation.surface: Fed up with the Spanish PM's spouse hosting.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of premier's just links.
explanation.definitionFit: A helpmate is a companion or partner, typically a spouse.

clue.text: Screen test where exposure prevails over justice?

definitions.meaning: whimsically, a trial run of a film or TV show
a staged trial whose public spectacle matters more than fair judgement

explanation.surface: An audition where publicity matters more than fairness.
explanation.walkthrough: Double definition of sorts: the first is whimsical.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigged public trial is put on for propaganda, with the verdict already decided.

clue.text: Unmask Tories perhaps there and then

parts.note: to out someone is to expose or unmask them
the Tories are an example of the political right

explanation.surface: A call to expose Conservatives on the spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks Tories as one example of the right wing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean immediately, at once, on the spot, without any delay.

clue.text: A pair of transmitters and convertor safely relocated

indicators.note: the letters are moved to new positions

explanation.surface: A pair of radio transmitters and a convertor moved safely.
explanation.definitionFit: The pair of cranial nerves that carry smell signals to the brain are sense transmitters.

clue.text: Ring head of state up, showing good judgment

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read bottom to top

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen as head of state
a sound person shows good judgement

explanation.surface: Phone the head of state; it shows good judgement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a phone call; it means echo.
explanation.definitionFit: To resound is to ring out or echo loudly.

clue.text: Smoothest tripe served up almost unsurpassed

indicators.note: in a down entry, served up means the letters rise, read backwards
the last letter is dropped

parts.note: bilge is nonsense, tripe
best means unsurpassed

explanation.surface: The finest tripe is the dish served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts BILGE to BILG, which 'served up' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Glib means fluent in a slick, superficial way, so the superlative is most smooth-talking.

clue.text: Showy TV full of error, beginning to end

indicators.note: the set is filled with the error, which sits inside

parts.note: telly is British slang for television

indicators.note: the first letter moves to the end

parts.note: a sin is a wrong or error

explanation.surface: Television full of mistakes, start to finish, is flashy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to end' moves S of SIN to the back, giving INS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinsel is cheap glitter, so something gaudy and flashy has that quality.

clue.text: Highly inaccurate description of pauper

definitions.meaning: a shot wide of the mark is well off target, whimsically read as poorly far away
a pauper is poor, lacking money

explanation.surface: A wildly wrong account of a poor man.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is whimsical: something badly off the mark is very inaccurate.
explanation.definitionFit: A pauper is impoverished, in poor financial circumstances, which the phrase describes.

clue.text: A singular gesture brings delegate

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
a sign is a gesture made with the hand

explanation.surface: One odd wave of the hand produces a representative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delegate' looks like a noun but works as the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To delegate a task is to hand it over or allot it to someone else, the verb sense.

clue.text: Isolated dispatch received by French company in recession

indicators.note: one thing is received inside another, so the dispatch goes within
receding means going back, so the company abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: Cie is the French abbreviation for compagnie
to remit is to send off or dispatch

explanation.surface: A lonely message arrives at a French firm during an economic downturn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in recession' reverses the company to EIC; 'Isolated' means living as a hermit, not cut off by economics.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to a hermit or recluse, living alone in solitude.

clue.text: Get wind of doctor breaking law

indicators.note: the doctor breaks into the law, splitting it apart

parts.note: a rule is a law
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: Finding out that a physician has broken the law.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, to rumble someone is to discover or see through their scheme.

clue.text: Specially adapted troops shadowed guards

indicators.note: the shadowing word surrounds and guards the troops

parts.note: to tail someone is to follow or shadow them
OR, other ranks, are ordinary troops

explanation.surface: Soldiers secretly followed the sentries, with special adjustment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guards' looks like a noun but is the containment verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made to measure for a particular purpose has been customised to fit.

clue.text: "Skinny" male swimming with pride

indicators.note: letters swimming about are rearranged

explanation.surface: A thin man swims with pride.
explanation.walkthrough: '"Skinny"' in quotes signals the jocular sense of relating to the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Epidermal means relating to the outer layer of the skin.

clue.text: Using last of inherited money, break the bank

indicators.note: only the final letter of each following word is used

explanation.surface: Spending the last of a legacy to clean out a casino.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break the bank' reads as a gambling phrase, but 'bank' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dyke is an embankment or wall built to hold back water.

clue.text: Overrule order in stopping assignation

indicators.note: stopping a gap means filling it, so the pieces go inside

parts.note: a date is an assignation
OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: A command intervenes to halt a lovers' meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrule is to override, to control and hold sway over others.

clue.text: Tipped favourites look to maintain the pace

indicators.note: tipped over, so the whole is read backwards

parts.note: pets are favourites
a peek is a look

explanation.surface: Racing tipsters' favourites look able to keep going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tipped favourites' suggests betting tips; 'Tipped' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep step is to walk in time, keeping pace with others.

clue.text: Support holiday deferment

definitions.meaning: a prop or brace, such as the rope holding a mast
a short visit or break spent somewhere
a postponement, as of an execution

explanation.surface: A support payment postponed for the holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a triple definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers a brace, a visit away from home, and a legal postponement.

clue.text: Comrades rolling up blue carpet

indicators.note: in a down entry, rolling up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: pals are comrades
down means sad, blue

explanation.surface: Comrades rolling up a blue rug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carpet' means to reprimand, not a floor covering.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, carpeting someone is to rebuke them sharply.

clue.text: Joining a presenter with hardly any foreign capital

parts.note: a DJ, disc jockey, presents music shows
a cent, a foreign coin, is barely any money

explanation.surface: An impoverished broadcaster with almost no foreign cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like a city; it is money.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjacent means next to or bordering, as things that adjoin.

clue.text: Notice investment of 50 made to settle account

indicators.note: to invest is to clothe or put inside, so the number is placed within

parts.note: to pay the bill is to settle an account
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A notice that fifty must be invested to clear a debt.
explanation.definitionFit: A playbill is a poster announcing a theatrical performance, a printed public notice.

clue.text: Italian dish from area south of local river supplied

indicators.note: in a down entry, south means lower, so it comes after

parts.note: the Po is the main river of Italy, local to the dish
lent means supplied

explanation.surface: An Italian meal sourced from land south of a nearby river.
explanation.definitionFit: A cornmeal porridge or cake eaten in northern Italy.

clue.text: Deceptively simple forces

indicators.note: the letters are not what they seem, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Forces that are deceptively simple, as physics often seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forces' looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or push someone into doing something.

clue.text: Former knight abandoning leader's standard

parts.note: ex- means former

indicators.note: the knight drops his first letter

parts.note: a Templar is a knight of the medieval crusading order

explanation.surface: A past knight abandoning his commander's flag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standard' looks like a banner but means a model.
explanation.definitionFit: An exemplar is a model or pattern to be copied, a benchmark.

clue.text: Temporary work on set?

definitions.meaning: standing in for now, as an interim chairman
performing as an actor on a film or stage set

explanation.surface: Temporary jobs fixing up a stage set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work on set' suggests carpentry; it is performance.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means serving temporarily, and also performing a role.

clue.text: A large deer in the midst of very small flies

indicators.note: the deer sits between the letters for very and small

parts.note: a moose is a large deer

explanation.surface: A huge deer in a swarm of tiny insects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flies' looks like insects but is the verb, to leave hastily.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for leaving quickly; to make oneself scarce is to bolt.

clue.text: Force displaying which female MP has issues

indicators.note: the phrase shows the letters within its text

explanation.surface: A female politician makes a forceful point on her problems.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress or weight put on something gives it force.

clue.text: Like croissant idiot picked up and consumed?

indicators.note: picked up by the ear, so the word for idiot is heard

parts.note: a loon is a foolish person
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: A fool grabbed a pastry and ate it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunate means crescent-shaped, the curve of a croissant.
